subject: Satyajit Ray
hook: Satyajit Ray pawned his wife's jewellery to keep filming.
twist: He risked everything to start his first film; at the end, the Academy's crew came to his Calcutta hospital bed to film his honorary Oscar speech, and he died 24 days later.
mood: Hand-printed Bengali woodblock meets monsoon watercolour: indigo, turmeric yellow, marigold orange and rain-grey washes on handmade rag paper, visible ink bleed and carved-line texture. Music: slow Bengali-inspired chamber piece, solo sitar and bansuri over soft tabla and tanpura drone, around 70 bpm, swelling gently at the hospital beat and ending on a single sustained note.
narration: Satyajit Ray pawned his wife's jewellery to keep filming. In nineteen fifty-two he began his first film, Pather Panchali. He had already borrowed against his insurance policy. By nineteen fifty-three, the money had run out. Shooting stopped for almost a year. Then the West Bengal government agreed to fund the film. The film was released in nineteen fifty-five. In nineteen ninety-two, the Academy honoured him for his rare mastery of the art of motion pictures. He was too ill to travel. Audrey Hepburn introduced him, and a crew filmed his thanks from a hospital bed in Calcutta. Twenty-four days later, he was gone. He once risked everything to begin. At the end, Hollywood came to him. Risk everything for art, or play safe?

captions.instagram_caption:
Satyajit Ray pawned his wife's jewellery to keep filming. 🎞️

In 1952 Ray began shooting his first film, Pather Panchali. He had already borrowed against his insurance policy, and from friends and relatives.

By 1953 the money had run out and shooting stopped for almost a year. Then the chief minister of West Bengal was approached, and the state government agreed to fund the film, paying in instalments.

The film was released in 1955, and Ray kept making films for decades.

In 1992 the Academy gave him an honorary award for his "rare mastery of the art of motion pictures". Too ill to travel, he thanked them on film from a hospital bed in Calcutta. He died 24 days after the ceremony.
